source_text: Omnis qui tetigerit carnes eius sanctificabitur. Contactus Christi sanctificat; contactus peccati polluit.
thought_title: Contact with Christ sanctifies, contact with sin pollutes
orientation: Origen is explaining the rule about eating the sin offering in the court, applying it to the soul's contact with Christ and with sin.
pass_a_gloss: Everyone who touches its flesh will be sanctified. Contact with Christ sanctifies; contact with sin pollutes.

choices.why: Passive future, matching the future force of the Leviticus rule.
The noun contactus takes an objective genitive; Christ is the one contacted.
Parallel construction to contactus Christi, with peccati as objective genitive.
Present tense, contrasting with the future sanctificabitur and the present sanctificat.

bible_refs.note: Omnis qui tetigerit carnes eius sanctificabitur

pass_b_english: Everyone who touches its flesh will be sanctified (Leviticus 6:27). Contact with Christ sanctifies; contact with sin pollutes.
